get_region_thickness — 2D features op

• Data kinds: region → feature

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "get_region_thickness", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: get_region_thickness (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*Knob a does not change the output (measured: identical at 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9).*

*Knob b does not change the output (measured: identical at 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9).*

Stages (the ops that come before → this op, left to right):

▸ get_region_thickness: stages (docs site)

Usage

An approximation of region thickness: `2 x max inscribed circle radius / max side length (twice the maximum of distance_transform_edt, normalized by the image size). Unlike HALCON's get_region_thickness` (Access the thickness of a region along the main axis.), which defines a 'thickness profile along the main axis,' this is a simplification that only looks at the direction-independent, global maximum inscribed radius (information about the main-axis direction is lost).
